chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari told us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jareer, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the sa'iba, so he said: A man frees his slave boy and says: 'Go where you wish, I have nothing to inherit from you, nor is there anything from your guilt upon me.' He said: And two witnesses testify.

key_terms.السَّائِبَة: A type of manumission where the freed slave owes no inheritance to the master and the master owes no blood-wit for him.
key_terms.جَرِيرَة: Guilt or liability, specifically referring to blood-wit (diyah) payable for killing.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and legal requirements of Sa'iba in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* clarifies the pre-Islamic and early Islamic practice of *sa'iba*, where a master frees a slave with the stipulation of mutual exemption from inheritance and blood-wit (*diyah*). It highlights the juristic requirement of two witnesses to validate this specific contractual manumission, reflecting the Shia emphasis on clear evidentiary standards in personal status law.
